metadata.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromised release
metadata.summary: Detects the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 Python package and the published affected OCI image digests without downloading or executing them.
metadata.author: PatchRover maintainers

sources.title: LiteLLM incident report: release v1.107.0 compromised

matchers.name: litellm
matchers.notes: Only an affected digest published in full is included. Prefix-only digests are intentionally excluded because they are not exact production indicators; version and tag evidence remains affected.

remediation.summary: Treat every environment that executed the affected package or image as compromised, rebuild from clean inputs, and rotate every reachable credential.
steps: Do not start Python or pip inside an affected environment because the malicious startup files can execute again.
Quarantine or destroy affected environments and rebuild images or virtual environments from clean inputs.
Pin LiteLLM to 1.106.2 or another explicitly confirmed safe release after reviewing the latest maintainer guidance.
Review cloud and identity logs for credential use outside the expected infrastructure.
tests: Build in a clean isolated environment and run the application test suite.
Verify the dependency lock and SBOM contain the reviewed safe version.
Verify no affected image digest or mutable incident-time tag is running.
operationalChecks: Observe the rebuilt image by immutable digest in every workload.
Confirm old replicas, jobs, rollback targets, nodes, caches, and registries cannot restart the affected artifact.
Complete credential rotation and incident review before declaring closure.
credentialRotation: Instance, task, or workload identity credentials reachable from the affected host.
AI provider, master, virtual, database, and environment credentials reachable by the affected process.
Any additional credential identified by the organization's incident-response investigation.
remediation.compromiseAssumption: If LiteLLM 1.107.0 or an affected image executed with outbound network access, assume reachable credentials were exfiltrated; absence of a marker file does not prove otherwise.

requirements: Observe an explicitly reviewed safe package version in source or the built artifact.
Observe a new immutable running image digest that does not match an affected digest.
Do not equate filesystem-indicator absence with absence of compromise.
Treat mutable tags without an observed immutable digest as unknown during verification.
